evidence.notes:
Design choices a reviewer may want to overrule:
1. Quality: I made quality:high inert (+0, reason line only) and added NO tie-break. Any depth-based tie-break can put a deeper model first on a tied score, which contradicts c2; the ticket said it 'may' break ties. Say so if you want a specific tie-break.
2. Cost with no preference is a sort tie-break (and the reason lines), not points, so on medium/large/unsized tickets a skill tag (+5) can still beat a cheaper tier at otherwise equal fit; micro/small tickets pay -8 per cost rank. An undeclared costTier ranks as normal. cost:low keeps its existing +10/-10 bonuses.
3. Score values changed: an over-capable model no longer sits at 50 (e.g. a deep model on a multi_step ticket scores 30). Anything that reads raw scores rather than order will see different numbers.
4. Escalation triggers on rejected and failed attempts only, using the latest such attempt even if a newer attempt is open (so while a retry runs, recommended still shows what the retry should have been). lease_expired, canceled, accepted and open attempts never escalate. 'Tier' = cost tier, then highest reasoning level, from the catalog only.
5. The recommended effort is moved onto an effort the model declares (next one up, else the highest below) with a reason, because claim_ticket refuses undeclared efforts (DM-24).
6. rankOf/highestLevel/REASONING_RANK moved from capabilities.ts into new modelTiers.ts so recommendation.ts can share them without a circular import.

RISKS AND FOLLOW-UPS (please read):
1. Dead end if an orchestrator ACCEPTS a node whose verdict failed (or named no increment): the gate reads the accepted attempt and an accepted ticket cannot be claimed again in the run, so increment_merged can never be met. The flow is: reject a failed submission with its reasons, then the node is resubmitted. docs/architecture.md and the submit_attempt description say so, but nothing enforces it. Suggested follow-up: make accept_attempt refuse an acceptance node whose standing verdict is missing or failed. I did not add it: it changes accept semantics and many existing flows accept nodes without increments.
2. reconcile_attempt 'resubmit' on an acceptance node stores no increment (it does not take one), so that node's gate stays unmet (fails closed). carry_forward of an acceptance node copies outputs but not the earlier increment, so it also leaves the gate unmet. outputs.summary:
The server now verifies, on submit, that a sprint landed on the epic branch as one squashed commit, stores the verdict, and gates the checkpoint on it.

What was built:
- Git adapter: read-only isAncestor(a, d) (git merge-base --is-ancestor; true/false/null when git cannot say) and commitParents(ref) ({commit, parents} via rev-parse --verify then rev-list --parents; null for an unknown commit, a range or garbage). The default runner now reports git's real exit status so a clean 'no' (1) differs from a failure.
- submit_attempt / submitAttempt take an optional increment { branch, commit } (acceptance nodes only; a work ticket that names one gets invalid_input; the schema is src/core/schemas.ts incrementRef). The command layer (src/core/commands/execution.ts) asks git, then submitAttempt stores the verdict in the new attempts.increment_json column (migration v6) in the same transaction as the submission. Verification is src/core/services/incrementVerify.ts and checks, in order: named branch equals the epic's own branch name; commit exists; exactly one parent; reachable from refs/heads/<epic branch>; after its base (not reachable from the previous sprint's verified increment, or strictly after the epic start commit for the first one); and no commit recorded by the sprint's accepted, current work attempts is reachable from the epic branch (proves squashed, not merged).
- New gate increment_merged right after acceptance_accepted, on sprints with an acceptance node. It reads the stored verdict of the node's standing attempt (accepted, else the one awaiting review); rejected or superseded attempts never count. Evaluation stays synchronous SQL.
- Views: AttemptView.increment, RunView.increments (get_run), SprintReportView.increment (get_sprint_report and the checkpoint's report; outside the content hash, so grants are unaffected). Run history exports attempts[].increment (optional, no default: legacyRecords tests pass unchanged, bytes preserved). MCP tool descriptions updated; SCHEMA_FINGERPRINTS: only submit_attempt changed, on purpose.

Decisions:
1. A failed verification STORES a failed verdict with reasons and does not reject the submission: the attempt stays submitted, the gate stays unmet, submit_attempt returns the reasons, and the orchestrator rejects the attempt and the node is resubmitted as a new attempt. Git not knowing the commit/branch is a failed check, never an error.
2. Epic branch with startCommit null and no earlier increment: the base check is recorded as 'skipped' with that reason (it cannot be proven), the verdict can still pass. Same for the squash check when the sprint's accepted work recorded no commit hash. Skipped checks never count against an increment. Documented in docs/architecture.md.
3. The verification measures against the epic's recorded branch, never the caller's; a submission naming another branch fails with that reason.
4. Base for sprint N is the nearest earlier sprint's verified increment in the run, else the epic start commit.

Existing tests changed because of the new gate: checkpointsAcceptance (condition lists, unmet ids), acceptanceGate integration (acceptance alone now leaves increment_merged unmet; the approvable-checkpoint flow is in incrementMerged.test.ts), migrations (v5 to v6 numbers), validation fingerprint, renderer fixtures (type-only: increments: [] and the new gate label). RISKS AND DECISIONS FOR THE REVIEWER.

1. COMPATIBILITY HAZARD (verified): the pre-sprint app's project schema is a strict object, so it REJECTS the seeded project.json ('Unrecognized key: definitionOfDone'; I ran HEAD's projectRecord against the new file). A Workspace opens its store by reading project.json, so the installed app/MCP server (which predates this sprint) will fail to open a checkout once this commit is merged into it. Do not merge the seed commit 4b535aa into the main checkout, or the live DM server's working tree, until the app that runs there has been rebuilt with this ticket. The seed is isolated in its own commit for that reason.

2. Orchestrator cannot set the DoD: authz.ts now splits PLANNER into PLANNER_SHARED + PLANNER_ONLY; the orchestrator keeps PLANNER_SHARED. The pattern in authz.ts is orchestrator = planner + extras, so this is a deliberate exception. Consequence: no single role lists every MCP tool any more, so server.test.ts's orchestrator rig lists all tools except set_definition_of_done (checked separately with a planner rig), and the runbook's 'orchestrator = everything a planner can' line was corrected.

3. Matching rule: trimmed + case-insensitive (checkNameKey), never by containment; DoD names must be unique under the same rule (schema refine), so a reported name maps to one check. A check passes when the evidence names it at least once AND every entry under that name is 'passed' (same rule a row check uses; failed outranks skipped in the reason).

4. No DoD = no gate (the condition is left out, so every existing test and checkpoint view is unchanged). The gate also exists only on sprints with an acceptance node, and the file is only read for such sprints.

5. Only the node's accepted, non-superseded attempt counts (not 'submitted', unlike increment_merged), per c3. The gate reads the live DoD at each evaluation, so a DoD edited mid-sprint applies to the sprint in flight (not pinned to the run). If project.json is invalid (e.g. merge markers), get_checkpoint/advance for a sprint with a node fails with the file's import_rejected error.

6. setDefinitionOfDone with an empty list removes the key (file returns to its earlier bytes). It writes the file only: nothing is committed.

7. Also done, small: 'setDefinitionOfDone' added to DESKTOP_COMMANDS (IPC allowlist, no UI); renderer fixture label for the new gate id (typecheck needed it); docs/architecture.md and docs/runbooks/mcp-setup.md updated; GateConditionId gains 'definition_of_done'.

Sprint reports gain an optional retro, the report view gains server-computed tier facts, and sprints with an acceptance node get a retro gate.

RETRO: submit_sprint_report accepts retro { delivered[{ticket,demo,evidence}], wentWell, wentPoorly, actions, discoveries[{title,body,ticket?}], leftovers[{ticket,reason}], tierFit[{ticket,verdict,note}] } (zod: sprintRetroInput in src/core/schemas.ts; every list optional, body/note default ''). A ticket is an id or display key (exact match); src/core/plan/retro.ts normalizeRetro resolves it against the run's pinned plan, stores the stable id, and refuses an unknown ticket with invalid_input naming the field (retro.leftovers[0].ticket). Any ticket of the pinned plan is accepted, not only the sprint's. get_sprint_report returns it as report.retro (null when none).

TIER FACTS: SprintReportView.tierFacts (src/core/plan/tierFacts.ts computeTierFacts), one entry per ticket of the sprint in sprint order: key, size, plannedLevel, plannedEffort (the ticket's own effort, null if unset), attempts[{attemptId,number,state,modelId,effort,label,fallback}], attemptCount, rejectionCount (rejected only), escalated. Computed on every read from the run's attempts and the run's host catalog (else the latest registered, as match_capabilities does); never stored, not in content hash. Only kind=work attempts count (carry_forward ran no worker); superseded attempts count (they ran). ESCALATION = some attempt used a higher model tier (compareTier: cost tier, then highest reasoning level; both models must be in the catalog) or a higher effort (both recorded) than some earlier attempt; either dimension is enough, later need not follow earlier directly, and a later drop does not undo it. FALLBACK/unranked: orchestrator-fallback attempts (modelId null, label 'Orchestrator (fallback)', now the shared constant ORCHESTRATOR_FALLBACK_LABEL) are listed with fallback:true, counted in attemptCount/rejectionCount, but never ranked (no model, no effort), so they cannot cause or hide an escalation; the ranked attempts around them are still compared. Models not in the catalog, or no catalog, are compared by effort only.

GATE: new GateConditionId 'retro' ('Sprint retro included'), only for sprints with an acceptance node, placed after the node gates (acceptance_accepted, increment_merged, definition_of_done) and before exit_criteria. Met when the latest report revision has a retro with at least one entry in some list (an empty retro {} is unmet: 'The Sprint N report's retro is empty'; none: 'The Sprint N report has no retro; resubmit it with retro {...}'). Only the latest revision counts, so a later revision without a retro puts it back to unmet, and the existing report-hash-bound approval does not carry over. Plans without nodes have no such gate.

Design decisions:

outputs.summary:
DM-40: approve the retro and the redraft in one step.

1. New gate `plan_current`, always present, placed last before `approval`. It is unmet while the epic's draft holds changes the saved plan lacks, or while a saved revision newer than the run's is not adopted. Its detail says: save and adopt the new revision, or discard the draft; or adopt revision N. An unchanged draft (same content hash as the saved plan, which is what save treats as `unchanged`) does not trip it. Because it is a gate, it also blocks advance_sprint under an authorized auto policy.

2. Report staleness. Schema v7 adds `sprint_reports.revision_id`, the plan revision the run executed when the report was submitted. It is local only and not exported. After an adoption, the pure function `sprintScopeChanges` (src/core/plan/sprintScope.ts) compares the sprint's exit criteria and required tickets between the report's revision and the run's revision. Removed tickets are allowed when they are retro leftovers or (transitively) require one, which is what redraft moves. Anything else makes `report_submitted` unmet with "... submit a new report revision". Reports with no recorded revision (pre-v7 or imported) count as current.

3. New desktop-only command `approveWithRedraft { runId, expectedDraftRevision, reportId? }`, service in src/core/services/approveRedraft.ts. It runs: save → adopt (skipped when the run already executes the saved plan) → recompute gates on the adopted revision → approve the current report → advance.
- The grant binds the adopted revision plus the report id and hash, and the advance consumes it.
- A redraft that added a sprint after the final one advances into it; the epic is not completed.
- Every refusal names its step: the message reads "Approve with redraft stopped at step N of 5 (<step>): ...", and details carry {step, stepNumber, savedRevisionId, savedRevisionNumber, adoptionNeeded}. The original code is kept; non-domain errors become `internal`.

Transaction design: the save commits on its own, because saving is two-phase:
- requestSave writes a pending revision and a snapshot outbox entry.
- The flush then writes the snapshot file, and the finalizer marks the revision saved and current.
- A file write can't be rolled back, and adoption only takes the epic's current saved revision.

The command therefore flushes (core.safeFlush) between the save and the rest; if the revision is still pending, the save step refuses with save_pending. Adopt, recompute, approve and advance then run in ONE db transaction. A refusal at any of them rolls all of them back: the run stays on its old revision with nothing approved or advanced, the saved revision stays current, and the error says "The draft is saved as revision N, but Run #R still executes revision M: adoption is still needed."

Before saving, it checks that the run is owned, awaiting its checkpoint, and that reportId (if given) is still the latest report.

Authorization: it requires checkpoint.approve (human-only) plus plan.save, run.adopt and checkpoint.advance, all checked before anything runs, so every agent role is refused before the save. COMMAND_CAPABILITIES maps it to checkpoint.approve. It is added to DESKTOP_COMMANDS and is not an MCP tool (server.test HUMAN_ONLY).

The get_checkpoint MCP description now mentions plan_current and stale reports.

content.summary:
Sprint 3, retro and redraft, is done. All 7 tickets are accepted, and the sprint lands as ONE squashed commit on `scrum-cadence`: d04409b37e3015590d8df68f53aff769a9bb7adc (parent 7018f56, no merge commits, identical to the sprint integration branch). The epic branch now holds exactly one commit per sprint: f8de0e6 (sprint 1), 7018f56 (sprint 2), d04409b (sprint 3). Nothing has been pushed or merged into main.

**Read first**
- The installed app and server (0.14.0, skills 1.2.0) predate this epic. This run therefore recorded effort, acceptance nodes, increments, the Definition of Done and the retro by convention, not through the server. Everything below was verified on a build of `scrum-cadence`, in scratch repositories.
- The report schema of the installed server has no `retro` field, so this sprint's retro is written out below in the sprint-reporter skill's structure.
- `npm test` exits 1 only on `fireguard/test/runnerTimeout.test.ts` (`spawn C:\Program ENOENT`, Windows path with a space). This is the same environmental failure accepted in sprints 1 and 2. The main suite passes: 271 files, 4990 tests.
- The acceptance round found that epic success criterion s2 was only partly met: effort was not shown on graph nodes. This was a gap from sprint 1. I rejected DM-45 attempt 1 so the round would close it; attempt 2 added effort to graph nodes, tests first. Every success criterion is now met.

## Sprint review: delivered, and how to see it
- **DM-38, retro on the sprint report:** `submit_sprint_report` takes a `retro`, and `get_sprint_report` adds server-computed `tierFacts`. A sprint with an acceptance node gets a `retro` gate. See `src/integration/sprintRetro.test.ts` and DM-45's `shots/dm-45/c6-main-epic-log.json`.
- **DM-39, redraft the next sprint:** `redraft_next_sprint` moves leftovers, with the tickets that require them, and adds discoveries as tickets. Moved tickets get a fresh retry budget on adoption, and validation now gives run-aware warnings. See `src/integration/redraft.test.ts` and `shots/dm-45/c2-c3-leftover-without-node-log.json`.
- **DM-40, one-step approval:** adds the `plan_current` gate, report staleness, and the desktop-only `approveWithRedraft` (save, adopt, recompute, approve, advance; each refusal names its step). See `src/integration/approveWithRedraft.test.ts` and `shots/dm-45/c1-c3-discovery-only-log.json`.
- **DM-41, checkpoint screen:** the screen reads demo first, then retro, then the redraft panel with "Approve retro & redraft". The completed-epic overview shows each sprint's retro. Screenshots: `shots/dm-41/a..d*.png` and, from the combined build, `shots/dm-45/screenshots/c4-1..c4-3*.png`.
- **DM-42, skills 1.5.0:** the skills teach the retro and redraft loop, including the route for a required leftover in a sprint with an acceptance node. `docs/architecture.md` documents the loop. The built MCP server serves the skills unchanged (`shots/dm-45/c5-mcp-skills-log.json`).
- **DM-80, Fireguard:** grade A, score 96 (`shots/fireguard-s3.json`). The s2 fix's tests graded A, score 99 (`shots/fireguard-s3-fix.json`).
- **DM-45, acceptance round:** a two-sprint scratch epic ran end to end (137 assertions, 0 failing), the Definition of Done was run, the s2 fix landed (c4d8865), and the sprint was squashed. Graph screenshots with effort: `shots/dm-45/screenshots-s2fix/`.

## Went well
- Every work ticket (DM-38 to DM-42) and DM-80 was accepted on its first attempt, with no escalations.
- DM-41 and DM-42 ran in parallel and merged cleanly. The combined suite was green at every merge: 4858, then 4958, then 4990 tests.
- DM-40, the deep ticket on the high tier, found the acceptance-node limitation before it shipped. DM-42 documented the route around it, and DM-45 proved that route end to end.
- The acceptance round did its job: it caught an epic-level gap from sprint 1 and closed it within this sprint.

## Went poorly
- The s2 gap (no effort on graph nodes) got past sprint 1's acceptance round (DM-43). It surfaced only at the end of the epic and cost one DM-45 rejection.
- My dispatch briefs said DM-38 and DM-39 ran on the high tier, but the attempt records show the normal tier. I corrected this in a comment; the records are right.
- Each heartbeat reset the lease to the 15-minute plan default instead of the claim's 4-hour lease, so workers had to heartbeat every 5 to 10 minutes.
- Fireguard took about 1h50m per run. DM-80 ran it twice, because the ticket's command lacked `--json` and text mode lists only 20 mutation survivors.
- In the common case, a required leftover in a sprint with an acceptance node, the one-step approval stops at its recompute step, and a six-step manual route is needed.

## Tier fit, from the attempt records
| Ticket | Size and level | Attempts | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| DM-38 | medium, multi_step | 1, normal tier | right-sized |
| DM-39 | medium, multi_step | 1, normal tier | right-sized |
| DM-40 | medium, deep | 1, high tier (the only deep-capable model) | right-sized |
| DM-41 | medium, multi_step | 1, normal tier (the matcher's pick) | right-sized |
| DM-42 | small, routine | 1, normal tier (overrode the matcher's low-tier pick, because the low tier was rejected on 3 of 5 earlier tickets) | possibly oversized; the low tier was not tried |
| DM-80 | small, multi_step | 1, normal tier | right-sized |
| DM-45 | medium, multi_step | 2, normal tier; attempt 1 was rejected for the s2 plan gap, not for capability | right-sized |

No claim could record an effort, because the installed server predates it.

## Discoveries (the redraft source)
Each of these is a follow-up below.
1. approveWithRedraft cannot handle a required leftover in a sprint with an acceptance node (DM-40).
2. heartbeat_attempt resets the lease to the plan default (DM-41, DM-45).
3. The `redraft_next_sprint` tool description tells the orchestrator to save and adopt, which the skill forbids (DM-42).
4. `tierFacts` are not readable before the first report revision (DM-42).
5. The Retry button is still offered for a leftover the redraft is moving, and there is no desktop button to redraft (DM-41).
6. The `get_checkpoint` description omits `definition_of_done` (DM-42).
7. A rejected acceptance node counts against `retryLimit`, and the skills don't say so (carried from DM-44).
8. Test hardening: mutation survivors in `services/attempts.ts` (35), renderer `workspaceActions.ts` and `EpicWorkspace.tsx` (38), and the join node's path arithmetic in `nodes.tsx` (5) (DM-80, DM-45).
9. The ts-prune baseline breaks on line drift and on the split between the web and node projects (DM-45).
10. `runnerTimeout.test.ts` fails on Windows (DM-45).
11. `pendingReason` counts superseded attempts (DM-39).

## Leftovers
None: every required ticket of sprint 3 is accepted.

## Actions for the next epic
- Rebuild and install the app from `scrum-cadence` before running another epic, so the server records effort, nodes, increments, the retro and redraft instead of relying on convention.
- Have acceptance rounds check each epic success criterion literally against the UI, starting in sprint 1.
- Give Fireguard tickets `npm run fireguard -- --json`, so one run is enough.
- Register every tool the host has (network, browser) before `start_run`.
- Keep the low tier for record and config edits only (profile proposal).
